heading: What's New in Murmur
skipped_one: Plus one more version you skipped: {{versions}}

0.18.0.title: Murmur for iPhone
0.18.0.text: Record and transcribe on your phone, offline, when your computer isn't at hand. Pair it here with a QR code: meetings move over the local network on their own, encrypted, the computer runs the final pass and the summary, and they come back to the phone revised. Look for Murmur on the App Store.

0.17.0.title: You choose what happens at the end
0.17.0.text: When a meeting ends or you open a file, you choose the steps: speakers, Whisper, punctuation and summary. Murmur remembers your choice, and whatever you leave for later is in the meeting's menu.

0.17.0.title: The calendar, on Windows and Linux too
0.17.0.text: Add the iCal link of a Google, Outlook or iCloud calendar and Murmur will remind you before each meeting, with its title and guests. On the Mac, it adds to the system's calendars.

0.17.0.title: System audio on Linux too
0.17.0.text: Murmur can now record what your computer plays, like the voices on a call, with PulseAudio or PipeWire, and keeps them apart from yours.

0.17.0.title: Summaries with Gemini or OpenRouter too
0.17.0.text: Besides Claude and OpenAI, you can now have Gemini or any of OpenRouter's models write the summary, with your own key. Pick the model with a search box.

0.17.0.title: No half-recorded meetings
0.17.0.text: While recording, your computer no longer goes to sleep. And if the microphone stops sending sound (a device change, headphones disconnecting), Murmur tells you right away and opens it again.

0.15.0.title: The graphics card, on Windows and Linux too
0.15.0.text: Whisper's final pass and the summary use your computer's graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), as they already did on the Mac. Nothing to set up: without one, or if the model doesn't fit, Murmur uses the processor as before.

0.15.0.title: Murmur for ARM PCs
0.15.0.text: There's a version for PCs with a Snapdragon, such as the Surface and Copilot+ PCs, that runs faster than the emulated one. If you already have Murmur on one of these PCs, download the ARM installer once; after that it updates itself.

0.14.0.title: Save meetings to Notion
0.14.0.text: Connect Murmur to Notion from the browser, with no key to create, and pick the page your meetings go under. They're saved from Export or on their own when they end, and only the text is sent.

0.14.0.title: And to Obsidian
0.14.0.text: If you use Obsidian, Murmur saves each meeting there as a note, with properties to filter by, tasks as checkboxes and the screenshots. By hand from Export or on its own when it ends.

0.14.0.title: Subtitles
0.14.0.text: Export › Subtitles saves the transcript as SRT or WebVTT, in short two-line cues, with the speaker's name if you like and in the translation if you made one. If the meeting came from a video, they're saved next to it with the same name.

0.14.0.title: Transcribe videos
0.14.0.text: Open or drop a video (mp4, mov, mkv, webm) and Murmur transcribes its sound, as with audio. Also from the Share menu and with Open With.

0.14.0.title: Tidier settings
0.14.0.text: The settings sections now sit in a sidebar, and Markdown has moved to the new Export section, alongside Notion and Obsidian.

0.13.0.title: Introduce yourself to Murmur
0.13.0.text: Say “Murmur, I'm Marta” during a meeting and that speaker becomes Marta. Handy when several people share one microphone. Works in Catalan, Spanish and English.

0.13.0.title: Murmur knows your voice
0.13.0.text: Read one sentence aloud and from then on Murmur labels you as “You” from the very first word, in every meeting. The voiceprint stays on your computer and you can delete it any time.

0.13.0.title: Anonymous statistics
0.13.0.text: To learn what to improve, Murmur sends anonymous usage data, such as how many meetings you have and how long they last, in ranges. Nothing that's said is ever sent, nor titles or names. You can turn them off in Settings › General.

0.12.1.title: Both Whispers, always in view
0.12.1.text: In Settings › Transcription › When Recording Ends you'll find the Catalan Whisper and the one for Spanish and English, each saying what it's for, and a switch to turn the Whisper pass off if you don't want it.

0.12.1.title: How often the glossary corrects
0.12.1.text: Next to each glossary word you'll see how many times it has corrected it, so you know which ones earn their place.

0.12.0.title: Murmur on Windows and Linux too
0.12.0.text: Murmur now runs on Windows and Linux as well, thanks to @xaviviro's work. The downloads are on the website, and they update themselves just like on the Mac.

0.12.0.title: A Whisper for Catalan
0.12.0.text: Meetings in Catalan are now listened to again by a Whisper from the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, the best in our tests for Central, Valencian and Balearic Catalan. If you have meetings in Catalan, download it (1.1 GB).

0.12.0.title: Translate the transcript
0.12.0.text: In the “···” menu, “Translate the transcript into” turns it into Catalan, Spanish or English with the summaries' model. The original stays as it is: you can switch back any time.

0.12.0.title: Choose the summary's language
0.12.0.text: Next to “Generate Again”, pick the language you want the summary in and Murmur writes it again.

0.12.0.title: Actions, in the “···” button
0.12.0.text: Continue Meeting, Transcribe again and Delete Meeting are now in the toolbar's “···” button, and Copy as Markdown and the audio, in Export. When a meeting finishes, the new text comes in as a light passes over it.

0.11.4.title: Merge two speakers
0.11.4.text: If Murmur has split one person into two speakers, open the name's menu and pick “All of …'s lines are…”. You can also rename one with the other's name.

0.11.4.title: Softcatalà's punctuation
0.11.4.text: Softcatalà's punctuation model can now be downloaded. It adds full stops, commas and capitals to meetings that mix Catalan and Spanish.

0.11.3.title: Summary and transcript, as two files
0.11.3.text: If you save each meeting as Markdown with “Everything”, you now get two files: one with the summary and notes, and another with the transcript.

0.11.3.title: Calendar connects in the background
0.11.3.text: When you connect your calendar, you can close Settings while macOS loads your accounts. An indicator at the bottom of the sidebar tells you when it's done.

0.11.1.title: Export just what you need
0.11.1.text: For Word and Markdown you can export everything, just the summary and notes, or just the transcript. Word files now include the summary too. And for Markdown saved automatically, you choose what goes in.

0.11.1.title: Indents in notes
0.11.1.text: Press Tab to indent a paragraph and Shift+Tab to undo it. In lists, Tab nests an item under the one above. Indents carry over to Word, Markdown and shared links.

0.11.0.title: Continue a meeting
0.11.0.text: If you stopped too soon, press “Continue” within the next 10 minutes, or choose “Continue Meeting” from the title menu. It all stays one meeting, with a line marking the pause.

0.11.0.title: The same voices
0.11.0.text: When you continue, Murmur recognises who had already spoken and keeps their name and colour. The audio stays in one file and the length is the sum of the parts.

0.10.0.title: Glossary
0.10.0.text: Add names and brands, and the transcript will spell them your way, in imported audio too. When you correct a name in a sentence, Murmur offers to add it.

0.10.0.title: Guests' names, spelled right
0.10.0.text: In a calendar meeting, the guests' names count as glossary, and the summary spells them right too.

0.9.1.title: Drag audio onto the window
0.9.1.text: Drop an audio or video file on Murmur's window and it transcribes it. While you drag it, the window shows whether it can open it.

0.9.0.title: Send audio to Murmur from other apps
0.9.0.text: Murmur is in the Share menu: pick an audio file in Finder, Messages or any app that shares files, and Murmur transcribes it. You can also use Finder › Open With or drop it on the Dock icon.

0.8.0.title: Transcribe from a file
0.8.0.text: With File › Transcribe from File… (⌘O) you can open an mp3, m4a, wav, ogg or any other audio file, and Murmur turns it into a meeting with speakers and the final pass. It works out the language by itself.

0.8.0.title: Murmur, from Claude too
0.8.0.text: Claude Desktop and Claude Code can read and search your meetings and transcribe audio on this Mac with Murmur. Audio never leaves the Mac.

0.8.0.title: A new mark
0.8.0.text: The two bars looked like a pause button. Now Murmur is an “m” and its echo: the voice and the transcript.

0.8.0.title: Clearer settings
0.8.0.text: There's a button to close them, and they say “Saved” each time you change something.

0.7.1.title: Bigger or smaller notes text
0.7.1.text: Use ⌘+ and ⌘− to change the size of the notes text, and ⌘0 to go back to normal. It's also in the View menu.

0.7.0.title: Every meeting as Markdown in your folder
0.7.0.text: Choose a folder and Murmur saves the summary, notes and transcript there when each meeting ends. While recording, you can turn it on or off from the top bar.

0.7.0.title: The cover is now called Summary
0.7.0.text: That's its name across the app and on shared pages. Exporting or copying as Markdown now includes the summary too.

0.7.0.title: A stop button that's easier to see
0.7.0.text: The button that stops the recording, in the top bar, is bigger and easier to spot.

0.6.0.title: Set up Cloudflare from Murmur
0.6.0.text: Open Cloudflare with the token ready, paste it, and Murmur publishes your sharing space there. No terminal needed.

0.6.0.title: Share screenshots and audio too
0.6.0.text: Choose what's included. Whoever opens the link can listen to the recording, jump to any minute and download it all as Markdown. Shared meetings show a link icon.

0.6.0.title: Transcribe again in another language
0.6.0.text: If you recorded in the wrong language, Whisper listens to it again in Catalan, Spanish or English, from the meeting's title menu.

0.5.0.title: Share a meeting with a link
0.5.0.text: Choose whether to share the cover, the notes or the transcript, when the link expires and whether it has a password. Murmur encrypts it on this Mac and publishes it on your Cloudflare account, which is free.

0.5.0.title: More reliable updates
0.5.0.text: The update package unpacks properly, and if something goes wrong, the window explains it without getting distorted.

0.4.0.title: Tags to organise your meetings
0.4.0.text: Add as many as you like under a meeting's title. You can filter by them in the sidebar and search for them. Right-click to rename, merge or delete them.

0.4.0.title: Choose before you start
0.4.0.text: When you start recording you can pick the language and say whether more people are in the room. If someone joins halfway through, you can change it without stopping the recording.

0.4.0.title: Covers by Claude or OpenAI too
0.4.0.text: With your own account and key, the cover is written in seconds and you can pick the model. Only the text is sent, never the audio. By default everything still happens on this Mac.

0.4.0.title: A handier recording bar
0.4.0.text: The screenshot is now the main button, and stopping a recording asks you to confirm. You can also export a meeting's screenshots.

0.4.0.title: One job at a time
0.4.0.text: While you're recording another meeting or on a call, Murmur waits before finishing the previous one, so your Mac doesn't slow down. Each speaker in a call also gets their own colour.

0.3.0.title: Meetings in Catalan, Spanish or English
0.3.0.text: Choose the language people speak. With “Catalan + Spanish” it understands both, even mixed in the same sentence.

0.3.0.title: Whisper goes over the transcript
0.3.0.text: If the meeting is in a single language, Whisper listens to it again when it ends and adds punctuation, capitals and properly spelled names. About 6 minutes per hour of meeting.

0.3.0.title: Murmur, now in Spanish and English too
0.3.0.text: The interface follows your system language. You can change it whenever you like.

0.3.0.title: The cover, in the language you choose
